**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), confidence 0.78.**

What I found in the licence grant (§2, p0028) and related clauses:

| Material term | Status |
|---|---|
| Affiliates | ✅ Covered expressly, no notice condition — better than fallback |
| Not revocable at will | ✅ Perpetual while fees paid (§17(a)); termination only for insolvency or 30-day uncured material breach (§17(c)(7)); converts to fully paid perpetual on Garman's default (p0128, p0115) |
| Contractors | ❌ Silent; §3(c) makes any sublicence subject to Garman's discretionary written consent |
| Transferable to successor | ❌ "non-transferable" grant, §3(c) assignment bar, and §20(d) consent requirement with no M&A carve-out |

Because the fallback expressly requires transferability to a successor in an M&A transaction and nothing in the document provides it, the clause fails the fallback on a material term. The redline (validated, `ok:true`) makes two minimal edits: adds "contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf" to the licensed user group in §2, and adds a mutual, consent-free successor-assignment carve-out to §20(d) that overrides §§2 and 3(c). The perpetuity and revocation points were noted as compliant rather than flagged, and the site/AS400 limits were left alone as part of the existing commercial bargain.
